summary: Bonner County, Idaho: 1934 10-foot L-4 lookout and 62-foot L-6 patrol tower, both gone by 1960; no source describes what remains or current access.

facts.status_note: Both towers were gone by 1960; no source describes what remains.

events.note: 10-foot pole L-4 lookout on the southwest summit
62-foot pole L-6 patrol tower about 1/4 mile east
Both towers gone by 1960; Forest Lookouts records 'Destroyed'

evidence.supports: built 1934; 10-foot L-4 on southwest summit; 62-foot L-6 patrol tower 1/4 mile east
evidence.quote: Established in 1934, a 10' pole L-4 was built on the southwest summit, while a 62' pole L-6 patrol tower was constructed 1/4 mile to the east.

evidence.supports: about nine miles north-northeast of Priest River

evidence.quote: 10′ Pole tower L-4 built on southwest summit.

evidence.supports: 62-foot L-6 patrol tower constructed 1934 about 1/4 mile east
evidence.quote: 62′ pole L-6 patrol tower constructed 1/4 mile to the east.

evidence.supports: filed under Destroyed/Removed; hike-in access tag

corrections.why: No source says abandoned. Forest Lookouts says 'Destroyed'; Idaho Fire Lookouts files the site under 'Destroyed/Removed' and says both towers were gone by 1960.

notes_for_editor: Correction proposed for the record's 1960 'abandoned' event; no source uses that word. The 1934 dates and the Priest Lake TPA agency agree across all three pages. Remains and current access are not described in any source read; the Hike-In tag on Idaho Fire Lookouts refers to the old site and is not an access ruling. Height: record height_m 3.0 is about right for a 10-foot pole (10 ft is about 3.05 m), so left unchanged and not repeated in facts. Staffing and fires are not documented in the sources read.
